Subject: 00UTO00000cRwzi2AC
Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Spoke with Sabrina, the manager. After several months of follow-up visits encouraging the shop to use EasyPay again, they are finally back on board and are now running EasyPay first. They are once again producing the same level of business they did with us when we were RIC, which is a great win.

This is a good example of how consistent relationship-building and periodic follow-up can help re-engage inactive merchants over time.

Sabrina shared that overall business has been slower, but higher repair costs have resulted in larger average ticket sizes, helping offset the decrease in car count. Based on their current activity, I estimate they have the potential to fund approximately $8K–$10K with EasyPay each month.

The shop is currently on a $20 spiff. Sabrina requested a poster, which I will provide once they are back in stock. I reminded her to reach out to Connor or me if she needs any assistance.

Full Comments:
Spoke with Shirley for an account review. She provided additional insight into the location's business model and customer base. Shirley explained that they service both local customers and dealership partnerships; however, the dealership-related work does not typically utilize EasyPay. When individual customers bring in their personal vehicles, financing is most commonly needed for repairs of $2,000 or more, at which point EasyPay is offered.

Shirley noted that business tends to slow down around rent-payment periods, with volume increasing once that timeframe has passed. She confirmed that EasyPay is their primary financing solution. While they do have another financing option available, it is a credit card program with a more complicated process, and they find EasyPay to be a much simpler and more effective solution for their customers.

No questions or concerns were reported, and the account remains engaged with the program.

Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Spoke with Catherine. She shared that the shop has been struggling over the past couple of months. Ever since ICE activity increased in Houston, they’ve seen a significant decline in business because many of their customers work in landscaping, roofing, construction, and other trades that rely on work trucks. She explained that many workers have been detained or are no longer working, so those trucks are not being used and therefore don’t need repairs.

She is hopeful that business will improve once school starts, as families may need to repair additional vehicles for their children or prepare their cars for the new school year. For now, the shop is simply waiting for business to pick back up.

Full Comments:
Called and spoke with Hamid, who was very friendly and conversational throughout the call. We discussed how business has slowed recently, with many customers either on vacation or preparing for the upcoming school season. Hamid also shared that he had recently returned to the U.S. after being stranded overseas during the conflict in the region and was grateful to be back.

Regarding the business, Hamid confirmed that they offer **EasyPay as their primary financing option**. They also have Snap Finance available, but they prefer to present EasyPay first because they like the platform better and have been happy with their overall experience.

I gathered updated shop potential, including an average repair order of **$1,500–$3,000**, an average of **three vehicles per day** during the current slow period, and **six service bays**.

I sent Hamid my direct contact information and encouraged him to reach out if he or his team has any questions or needs assistance in the future.

Help your customers get EasyPay texts again
 

 



If a customer stopped EasyPay texts, they can text START to 619-327-9835 to start getting them again.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Help Your Customers Get Our Texts Again
 
 
 
 Hello, 
 Text messaging runs through a long chain of carriers, apps, and filtering systems, and more of them are applying automated opt-outs on a customer’s behalf without notifying the sender.
 If a customer ever replied STOP, blocked our number, or was opted out automatically, they stop getting EasyPay texts – including the application link you send at the counter. Getting them reconnected takes one quick text.
 
 
 
 To Reconnect, Just Text
 START
 to
 619-327-9835
 One text and they’re reconnected right away – no forms, no calls, no waiting.
 
 
 
 How you can help:
 

 
 
 
 ✓

Brian shared that there is little perceived demand for financing, despite average repair orders starting around $500 and reaching up to $9,000. Marketing materials were also declined, as they have sufficient inventory. Merchant also offers Snap Finance, but Brian indicated it sees similar usage, as customers are generally not requesting financing regardless of provider. Opportunity remains to build financing awareness and strengthen credit culture over time.

Checked in via Maps Application 
I spoke with Jose, the owner of the furniture store. We recently got his account set up, and over the weekend he submitted several applications. Unfortunately, only one customer was approved, while the rest were declined.

I told him I would look into the declines and see if there was anything I could do, but he expressed frustration with the approval rates. He explained that they initially gave EasyPay the first opportunity on every financing request, but after seeing so many declines, they have started using other financing providers instead.

Jose specifically mentioned that three customers who were declined by EasyPay were later approved by Snap. As a result, he told me that if approval rates do not improve, they will continue relying on competitors that are approving more of their customers. This account has strong potential, but improving approvals will be critical to maintaining and growing its usage.
